In this paper we investigate the generalization capability of state-of-the-art object detection models
(Hi-SAM, YOLO, and RT-DETR) for the automatic segmentation of text lines in historical documents.
Generalization is needed because it is not practical for museums and archives to produce large
amounts of labeled samples for each new collection. We also evaluate the few-shot setting by fine-
tuning the networks with only a small number of training samples per target dataset. To this end,
we use nine different datasets that differ significantly in visual layout and language. Additionally,
we discuss why mean average precision (mAP), a classic evaluation metric for object detection, is
insufficient for assessing the quality of a text line segmentation model. Depending on the dataset,
our CRNN models achieve character error rates (CER) ranging from 2.48% to 7.07% per page for

CER= S+I+DN ,(1)
which is based on the Levenshtein edit distance [14]. CER quantifies the number of character-level operations required
to transform the predicted text into the ground-truth. It is computed as the ratio of the total number of substitutions (S),
insertions (I), and deletions (D) edits to the number of characters (N) in the ground-truth. Lower CER values indicate
better recognition performance, reflecting fewer discrepancies between the predicted and reference text.

BothYOLOv8andRT-DETRwere trained for up to 5,000 epochs with early stopping (patience = 250) using the
MuSGD optimizer (LR 0.01, momentum 0.9), batch size of 8, and an input size of 1280 × 1280 pixels.
To ensure a fair comparison, Hi-SAM was initialized using SAM pre-trained weights derived from natural-image
training, whereas YOLO and RT-DETR were initialized using weights pre-trained on the COCO dataset. As RT-DETR
produces only bounding-box predictions, the segmentation masks generated by Hi-SAM and YOLO are converted into
bounding boxes to enable a consistent comparison across models.
We observed that RT-DETR creates an extensive amount of overlapping predictions. To mitigate this issue, we apply
additional NMS as a post-processing step to remove redundant detections at inference.

For each dataset, we train a CRNN HTR model using text lines obtained from the ground-truth bounding boxes together
with their corresponding transcriptions. The CRNN models are trained using the Adam optimizer with a batch size of
32 and a learning rate of 5e-4. The training is conducted for 1,500 total epochs. The learning rate is reduced to 5e-5
with a patience of 100 and early stopping is applied with a patience of 200 after the learning rate drop.

dataset.
The experiments conducted here have primarily focused on documents with a rather simple layout: single-column text
arranged in neat horizontal lines with minimal marginalia. Detecting and recognizing more complex layouts, such as
those with curved or rotated text lines or tabular structures, increases the complexity of the problem. This issue will be
examined in greater detail in future research.
In this study we focused on the generalization capabilities of text line segmentation models. However, these models
constitute only the first step in an HTR pipeline. Therefore, further research to investigate and develop domain
adaptation and generalization for HTR models to determine and reduce the effort required for data acquisition in this
context is also needed.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream CRNN Character Error Rate (CER) computed against ground-truth transcriptions provides an independent measurement of segmentation quality and corroborates the headline findings, including the mAP limitation and few-shot gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by mAP50:95 on held-out test splits and, critically, by Hungarian-matched downstream CER from a separately trained CRNN HTR model evaluated against ground-truth transcriptions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Detector training and checkpoint selection used supervised segmentation losses and validation mAP on source or target-domain annotated pages.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims closely match the empirical evidence: Hi-SAM provides superior zero-shot transfer while YOLO matches it with minimal target supervision, and runtime/memory tradeoffs across CPU/GPU setups are clearly measured [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0048, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0055, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0065].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is solid, examining nine historical datasets across English, Norwegian, Swedish, and German in zero-shot cross-dataset transfer and 10/50-shot fine-tuning settings [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0016, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0040, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0048, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0053, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0055]. The authors effectively demonstrate that bounding box mAP is poorly correlated with downstream CER and that lightweight models like YOLO catch up to larger foundation models with minimal few-shot supervision [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0046, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0056].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream CRNN Character Error Rate (CER) evaluated against ground-truth transcriptions independently corroborates line segmentation quality and highlights mAP limitations [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0048, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0055].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Mean average precision (mAP50:95) on held-out test splits, alongside Hungarian-matched downstream Character Error Rate (CER) computed with an independent CRNN text recognition model [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0025, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0026, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0048].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised bounding box and segmentation losses (and validation mAP for model checkpoint selection) on source or target-domain annotated pages [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0034, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0038].

primary.limitations: The study explicitly acknowledges that evaluation was restricted to predominantly single-column, horizontal historical layouts without complex marginalia or tabular structures, and that HTR domain adaptation itself was kept constant rather than jointly adapted [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0068].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the training and fine-tuning protocols for the detectors across diverse historical datasets, the configuration of the downstream CRNN HTR model, and the Hungarian matching algorithm used to align predicted boxes to ground truth lines for CER computation [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0027, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0034, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0036, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0039].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-controlled comparative study addressing a practical question in document analysis and digital humanities. Experimental controls, baselines, and downstream validation metrics are sound and properly interpreted.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper investigates the cross-domain generalization and few-shot adaptation capabilities of modern object detectors (Hi-SAM, YOLOv8-seg, and RT-DETR) for historical handwritten text line segmentation, analyzing detection metrics (mAP) versus downstream recognition performance (CER) and benchmarking compute requirements across hardware setups [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0003, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0009, E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0065].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-controlled comparative study addressing a practical question in document analysis and digital humanities. Experimental controls, baselines, and downstream validation metrics are sound and properly interpreted.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The study explicitly acknowledges that evaluation was restricted to predominantly single-column, horizontal historical layouts without complex marginalia or tabular structures, and that HTR domain adaptation itself was kept constant rather than jointly adapted [E330ea45eb35e4bf9-B0068].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
